quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If you cannot see clearly, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Pass through carefully and do not stare at the work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass through carefully and do not stare at the work.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down or stare at construction work. This causes traffic jams. Drive through the zone normally and safely.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: To allow other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
To give the truck driver enough room to stop.
To allow other drivers to slow down safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give the truck driver enough room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does excessive speed do?

options.text: Gets you to your destination faster.
Helps you go around obstacles more easily.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of serious accidents. It does not save time and often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: What should you do when entering an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.
questions.explanation: Use the merge lane to speed up and smoothly blend with fast-moving traffic. Do not stop like you would on other roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Roadwork or maintenance is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs mark construction and maintenance work areas. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Traffic fines may be doubled in these areas.

questions.question: If water on the road causes your vehicle to lose grip, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a steady speed to get better grip.
Brake hard to stop your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: This is called hydroplaning. Your tires lose contact with the road and float on water. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not brake.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either side.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe if you take the right amount.
Prescription medicines are always safe to take.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines, prescription or over-the-counter, can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you tired. Know how your medicine affects you before driving.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for traffic, and go with caution.

questions.question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels. This makes you lose the ability to steer. To avoid this, drive at a safe speed for the conditions.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Other drivers whose vehicles have broken down on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
questions.explanation: You must obey flaggers at construction sites. They direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly so you can see clearly. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your mirror.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You may see this sign at busy intersections with heavy traffic.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down for curves and other conditions. You can drive slower than the speed limit, but never faster. Slow down for curves, hills with poor visibility, wet roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Lower your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas, do not use the brakes, stay in your lane, and let the car slow down on its own.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?
questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other roads. They can be icy even when the rest of the road is dry. Bridges also thaw out later than regular pavement.

questions.question: When parked facing uphill with no curb, set the brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels to the right (toward the edge) when parked uphill with no curb. This helps the car roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You should stop for other traffic.
Traffic is merging in from another road. Give them space to safely enter traffic.
Traffic is merging in from another road. Stay in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging in from another road. Give them space to safely enter traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will merge onto your road. Check your mirrors and sides, then move to another lane if possible to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: The lane to the right may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: At a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.10 percent, you are ____ times more likely to cause an accident than a sober driver.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seven
questions.explanation: A driver with a BAC of 0.10 percent is seven times more likely to crash than a sober driver. At a BAC of 0.15 percent, the risk is 25 times higher. At 0.17 percent, the risk is 50 times higher.

questions.question: In rain or fog, you should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and reduce visibility.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unpredictable conditions. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: A major cause of fatal traffic accidents in Tennessee is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding.
questions.explanation: Driving faster than the safe and legal speed limit is a major cause of fatal crashes in Tennessee.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is permitted when it's safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted when it's safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions. You may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: In rain or fog, you should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see your vehicle better.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Have one rear wheel touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave your vehicle in "park" when parking on a hill. Turn your front wheels away from the road center if there is no curb. If there is a curb, turn toward it when facing downhill, or away from it when facing uphill.

questions.question: Children under age ____ must use an approved child restraint device in a moving vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Children under 1 year old or under 20 pounds must use a rear-facing restraint. Children 1-3 years old and over 20 pounds must use a forward-facing restraint. Children 4-8 years old and under 4'9" tall must use a booster seat with a seat belt.

questions.question: When behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Keep a 3-4 second distance behind motorcycles. They can stop quickly and may fall. A larger distance protects both riders and motorists, especially on wet roads, gravel, or metal surfaces.
